author: goldturtle
body:
@marcfeuermann @pgaudet: submitted with the PAINT issue template's fields. The posting account cannot set labels, so please add `PAINT annotation`.

* **PTHR ID & PTN node:** PTHR46874; PTN002930185 (gain of negative regulation of apoptotic process, GO:0043066)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):** UniProtKB:P25445 FAS (Fas cell surface death receptor)

* **Type of Issue:** Erroneous source: the only source annotation describes Fas B, a soluble isoform that acts against full-length Fas.

*How this draft was made:* an automated screen compared every PAN-GO (IBA) annotation of human genes (release 2025-10-12_2.0.5, PANTHER 19) with the genes' experimental annotations in GO release 2025-10-10. Flagged annotations were then judged by evidence-cited reasoning (Claude subagents, citing only a curated evidence pack). The statements below were checked against the GO, PAN-GO and PANTHER data, and the papers behind the key annotations were read. Please treat it as a candidate for curator review.


**Inherited:** FAS `involved_in` *negative regulation of apoptotic process* ([GO:0043066](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0043066))

- **Gain:** PTN002930185 (speciation, Euteleostomi; human genes below: FAS), dated 2020-02-27.
- **Evidence genes (1):** Fas (MOUSE).
- **Relation to FAS:** orthologs: Fas (MOUSE).
- **Other human genes inheriting it:** none.
- **Losses of this term in the family:** none.
- **v1 (paper release):** same annotation, from PTN002930185.

**FAS's own experimental annotations** (GO release 2025-10-10) against *negative regulation of apoptotic process*: 3 opposing, 0 supporting:

- *positive regulation of apoptotic process* ([GO:0043065](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0043065)): [PMID:20935634](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20935634/) (IMP), [PMID:21625644](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21625644/) (IDA)
- *positive regulation of apoptotic signaling pathway* ([GO:2001235](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:2001235)): [PMID:11096076](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11096076/) (IMP)

**Literature (Textpresso, all species corpora):** 31 sentences mention FAS together with *apoptotic process*. By cue words, 20 describe the opposite of the inherited direction and 4 agree.

> Consistently, immunostaining indicates a cytosolic co‐localization of these two molecules (Figure 4I). **As aforementioned, FAS membrane translocation is a key event in FAS‐mediated apoptotic pathway.** We then wondered if PIR influences membrane distribution of FAS.

— Ma H, Suleman M, Zhang F, Cao T, Wen S, Sun D et al. (2024). Pirin Inhibits FAS-Mediated Apoptosis to Support Colorectal Cancer Survival. *Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany)*. [PMID:38148593](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38148593/).


> The DISC comprises an adaptor molecule, FADD (Fas-associated death domain), and the initiator caspase 8. **Two types of cells have been described in terms of CD95/Fas-induced apoptotic signalling.** In cells classified as type 1, Fas activation leads to caspase recruitment to the DISC in quantities that result in the activation of caspase 3, resulting in an apoptotic response that does not require mitochondrial function.

— Franklin-Tong VE, Gourlay CW (2008). A role for actin in regulating apoptosis/programmed cell death: evidence spanning yeast, plants and animals. *The Biochemical journal*. [PMID:18613816](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18613816/).


**Sentences counted as agreeing** (4): one is relevant: it reports an anti-apoptotic FAS splice isoform in chordoma. The other three are about FAS apoptosis inhibitory molecules, non-apoptotic CD95 signalling, and an experimental set-up.

> The dysregulation of one or more of those mechanisms during development and later in chordoma might be the cause of FAS/FASL altered expression. **In turn, a dysregulation of FAS alternative splicing is caused also by the enhanced expression of the anti-apoptotic FAS isoform in chordoma.** This study provides new insights on notochord biology and indicates the implication of Fas/Fasl in chordoma, addressing future areas of investigation to identify new targets for chordoma treatment and diagnosis.

— Ferrari L, Pistocchi A, Libera L, Boari N, Mortini P, Bellipanni G et al. (2014). FAS/FASL are dysregulated in chordoma and their loss-of-function impairs zebrafish notochord formation. *Oncotarget*. [PMID:25071022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25071022/).


**Reasoning** (evidence-cited; verdict *error likely*, medium confidence; cause: ortholog annotation conflict): FAS inherits 'negative regulation of apoptotic process' from a single mouse Fas annotation, yet FAS's own experiments from at least seven papers, a GO-CAM model and many sentences show it as a death receptor that triggers and promotes apoptosis. The only anti-apoptotic hints are a specific splice isoform and non-apoptotic signaling, which do not justify a general anti-apoptotic annotation for the gene.

- *Against:* FAS has IMP and IDA annotations from three separate papers to positive regulation of apoptotic process or of apoptotic signaling, the opposite direction. ([PMID:20935634](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20935634/); [PMID:21625644](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21625644/); [PMID:11096076](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11096076/))
- *Against:* FAS has further IDA/IMP annotations from four papers placing it directly in apoptosis and the extrinsic death-receptor apoptotic signaling pathway, and a GO-CAM model shows its receptor activity driving FASL-induced apoptosis. ([PMID:9681877](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9681877/); [PMID:12221075](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12221075/); [PMID:9333124](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9333124/); [PMID:22891283](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22891283/); gomodel:663d668500001551)
- *Against:* Literature consistently describes the Fas/FasL system as an apoptotic mechanism, including in lpr mutant mice. (Ma et al. 2024; Nat Rev Immunol highlights 2002; Liu W et al. 2015; Wajant 2003)
- *For:* An anti-apoptotic FAS splice isoform is reported in chordoma, indicating an isoform-specific opposite effect. (Ferrari et al. 2014)
- *Context:* Fas can also signal non-apoptotically (proliferation, NF-kappaB activation, inflammation), but these reviews do not describe it as inhibiting apoptosis. (Wajant et al. 2003; Le Gallo et al. 2017)
- *For:* The inheritance rests on one ortholog, mouse Fas, at a speciation node and was already in v1. (Fas; PANTHER tree; PAN-GO v1)

*Reasoner's suggested fix:* Review the mouse Fas source annotation to negative regulation of apoptotic process; if it is context- or cell-type-specific, remove the gain of [GO:0043066](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0043066) at PTN002930185 or add a loss at PTN000559235. *Tree check:* A loss at PTN000559235 sits directly below ortholog evidence (Fas (MOUSE)): a conflict with orthologs, so review that annotation first.

**Suggested change:**

- *negative regulation of apoptotic process* rests on Fas (MOUSE), orthologs whose annotations conflict with FAS's own experimental annotations and the literature. Review those source annotations, or whether this term should propagate, rather than adding a loss.
- The mouse Fas source annotation (IDA, acts upstream of or within; [PMID:7595210](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7595210/)) concerns Fas B, a soluble splice isoform that blocks Fas ligand-induced apoptosis. Human FAS has a TAS to the same term ([PMID:7510905](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7510905/)) from a paper on a soluble human Fas isoform that blocks anti-Fas-induced apoptosis. Both describe an isoform acting against full-length Fas, so they are a weak basis for propagating the term to the gene.

### References
- Ferrari L, Pistocchi A, Libera L, Boari N, Mortini P, Bellipanni G et al. (2014). FAS/FASL are dysregulated in chordoma and their loss-of-function impairs zebrafish notochord formation. *Oncotarget*. [PMID:25071022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25071022/).
- Franklin-Tong VE, Gourlay CW (2008). A role for actin in regulating apoptosis/programmed cell death: evidence spanning yeast, plants and animals. *The Biochemical journal*. [PMID:18613816](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18613816/).
- Le Gallo M, Poissonnier A, Blanco P, Legembre P (2017). CD95/Fas, Non-Apoptotic Signaling Pathways, and Kinases. *Front Immunol*. [PMID:29021794](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29021794/).
- Liu W, Xu C, Zhao H, Xia P, Song R, Gu J et al. (2015). Osteoprotegerin Induces Apoptosis of Osteoclasts and Osteoclast Precursor Cells via the Fas/Fas Ligand Pathway. *PloS one*. [PMID:26571489](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26571489/).
- Ma H, Suleman M, Zhang F, Cao T, Wen S, Sun D et al. (2024). Pirin Inhibits FAS-Mediated Apoptosis to Support Colorectal Cancer Survival. *Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany)*. [PMID:38148593](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38148593/).
- Nature Reviews Immunology research highlights (2002). Textpresso document AGRKB:101000000830868 combines several highlights, and its record names only one of them (Alfred J, "C. elegans - an innate choice?"), which is not the source of the sentences cited here. Not in PubMed.
- Wajant H (2003). Death receptors. *Essays Biochem*. [PMID:14585074](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14585074/).
- Wajant H, Pfizenmaier K, Scheurich P (2003). Non-apoptotic Fas signaling. *Cytokine Growth Factor Rev*. [PMID:12485619](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12485619/).
title: PAINT issue: PTHR46874: FAS inherits "negative regulation of apoptotic process", contrary to its own experimental annotations
